NVIDIA and Oracle Expand NVIDIA Vera Rubin to Multi-Gigawatt Scale and Bring NVIDIA Vera CPU to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and NVIDIA Vera CPUs Are Now Generally Available on OCI, With Plans to Introduce HGX Rubin NVL8 Systems to Help Organizations Accelerate Frontier Model Training, Improve Inference Efficiency and Scale Agentic Workloads October 27, 2026 NVIDIA and Oracle today announced plans to expand Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Superclusters with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems to multi-gigawatt scale, supporting growing customer demand for AI training, inference and agentic applications. Oracle and NVIDIA also expanded their AI infrastructure collaboration with the general availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and NVIDIA Vera CPUs on OCI. The expanded collaboration gives customers infrastructure for both the GPU-intensive work of training and serving frontier models and the CPU-intensive tasks agents perform between model calls, including executing tools, testing code and retrieving data. Customers can scale CPU and GPU resources independently to match their workloads, helping reduce idle capacity and put more of their infrastructure to productive use. OCI Superclusters Help Organizations Bring Frontier AI to Market Faster at Multi-Gigawatt Scale OCI Superclusters combine NVIDIA NVL72 rack-scale systems, Oracle Acceleron networking with NVIDIA Spectrum-X ™ Ethernet networking featuring NVIDIA Spectrum™-6 switches and NVIDIA BlueField®-4 DPUs, and gigawatt-class power and cooling to train and serve the largest AI models.
